note: StewardMD original teaching animations (animated WebP, loaded from R2 when the app is built with SMD_REMOTE_MEDIA=1), AI-generated with Google Gemini (Nano Banana) 2026-11. One file serves every module that teaches the topic.

items.title: Immune response
items.caption: A purple dendritic cell picks up an amber antigen, carries it to a lymph node and shows it to a T cell; the T cell activates a B cell, which becomes a plasma cell releasing Y-shaped antibodies that stick to the antigen.

items.title: Acute inflammation
items.caption: A small blood vessel widens and becomes leaky; white neutrophils roll along the wall, stick, squeeze through the wall and move toward amber bacteria in the tissue.

items.title: Sepsis
items.caption: Amber bacteria in the blood release toxins, white cells release a burst of cytokines, the vessels dilate and leak fluid, and a blood pressure gauge needle falls.

items.title: Types of shock
items.caption: Four panels in a 2x2 grid around one heart and vessel diagram: hypovolaemic (vessels empty), cardiogenic (heart pumps weakly), distributive (vessels widen), obstructive (blood blocked before the heart).

items.title: Noradrenaline on alpha-1 receptors
items.caption: Teal noradrenaline binds purple alpha-1 receptors on the smooth muscle around an artery; the muscle contracts and the artery narrows.

items.title: Adrenaline receptor effects
items.caption: Teal adrenaline spreads to three targets in turn: the heart beats faster and stronger (Beta-1), the airways widen (Beta-2), the skin vessels narrow (Alpha-1).

items.title: Corticosteroid action
items.caption: A teal steroid molecule passes through a cell membrane, binds a purple receptor in the cytoplasm, moves into the nucleus and switches on genes, and fewer inflammatory signals leave the cell.

items.title: HPA axis
items.caption: Hypothalamus releases CRH, the pituitary releases ACTH, the adrenal cortex releases cortisol, and cortisol travels back to switch both off (negative feedback arrows).

items.title: Thyroid axis
items.caption: Hypothalamus releases TRH, pituitary releases TSH, the thyroid releases T4 and T3, which loop back to switch both off.

items.title: Thyroid hormone synthesis and carbimazole
items.caption: Inside a thyroid follicle, amber iodide is trapped and joined onto thyroglobulin by purple thyroid peroxidase to form T4 and T3; teal carbimazole binds thyroid peroxidase and production stops.

items.title: Levothyroxine action
items.caption: Teal levothyroxine (T4) travels in the blood, enters a tissue cell, is converted to T3 and binds a purple receptor in the nucleus, and the cell's metabolism speeds up (glowing mitochondria).

items.title: Cell cycle and chemotherapy
items.caption: A cell cycle wheel turning through G1, S, G2 and M; teal drug markers appear at the phase they act on: methotrexate at S, vincristine at M, cyclophosphamide damaging DNA.

items.title: Metastasis
items.caption: Tumour cells break through the basement membrane, enter a blood vessel, travel, leave the vessel and form a new tumour in a distant organ.

items.title: Ischaemic stroke core and penumbra
items.caption: A clot lodges in the middle cerebral artery; a dark core of dead brain forms with a glowing amber penumbra around it that slowly shrinks into the core.

items.title: Thrombolysis with alteplase
items.caption: Teal alteplase binds the clot surface, converts plasminogen into plasmin, the fibrin mesh dissolves and blood flows through the artery again.

items.title: Pneumonia consolidation
items.caption: A cluster of alveoli: amber bacteria enter, the air sacs fill with white cells and fluid, and oxygen bubbles can no longer cross into the capillaries (consolidation).

items.title: Anaphylaxis and mast cells
items.caption: Amber allergen cross-links IgE antibodies on a purple mast cell; the mast cell bursts open releasing histamine granules; then vessels leak and airways narrow.

items.title: Proton pump inhibitor
items.caption: A stomach parietal cell with a purple proton pump pushing amber H+ ions into the stomach; teal omeprazole binds the pump and acid output stops.

items.title: Insulin secretion and sulfonylureas
items.caption: In a pancreatic beta cell, amber glucose enters, ATP rises, a purple potassium channel closes, calcium flows in and insulin granules are released; then teal gliclazide closes the same channel directly.

items.title: NSAIDs and COX
items.caption: Amber arachidonic acid enters purple COX-1 and COX-2 enzymes and comes out as prostaglandins; teal ibuprofen blocks both enzymes and prostaglandin output stops.

items.title: Aspirin on platelets
items.caption: A platelet makes thromboxane through purple COX-1 and sticks to other platelets; teal aspirin permanently blocks COX-1 and the platelets stay apart.

items.title: Heparin and antithrombin
items.caption: Teal heparin binds purple antithrombin, which then grips thrombin and factor Xa much faster, switching them off.

items.title: Statin action
items.caption: In a liver cell, purple HMG-CoA reductase makes cholesterol; teal atorvastatin blocks it, the cell adds more LDL receptors to its surface and pulls amber LDL out of the blood.

items.title: Opioids and naloxone
items.caption: A pain signal travels across a synapse; teal morphine binds purple mu receptors, the signal fades; then teal naloxone knocks morphine off the receptors and the signal returns.

items.title: Neuromuscular junction, rocuronium and sugammadex
items.caption: A nerve ending releases amber acetylcholine onto purple nicotinic receptors and the muscle fibre contracts; teal rocuronium blocks the receptors and the muscle relaxes; teal sugammadex wraps the rocuronium and contraction returns.

items.title: Local anaesthetic
items.caption: An action potential runs along a nerve axon through purple sodium channels; teal lidocaine enters and blocks the channels and the signal stops at that point.

items.title: Chronic kidney disease
items.caption: A kidney with many nephrons; glomeruli scar one by one and turn grey, the remaining ones swell and work harder, and the kidney shrinks.

items.title: Paracetamol overdose and acetylcysteine
items.caption: In a liver cell, paracetamol forms toxic NAPQI, glutathione mops it up until it runs out and the cell is damaged; teal acetylcysteine refills glutathione and protects the cell.

items.title: Spironolactone
items.caption: In the collecting duct, aldosterone binds its purple receptor and the cell pulls amber sodium in and pushes potassium out; teal spironolactone blocks the receptor.

items.title: Tamsulosin
items.caption: An enlarged prostate squeezes the urethra; teal tamsulosin binds purple alpha-1A receptors in the prostate smooth muscle, the muscle relaxes and urine flows freely.

items.title: Peristalsis
items.caption: A wave of muscle contraction travels along a segment of bowel, pushing a food bolus forward, with ring muscle squeezing behind and relaxing ahead.

items.title: Nitrates (GTN)
items.caption: Teal GTN releases nitric oxide, vein walls relax and widen, less blood returns to the heart, and the heart's workload falls.

items.title: Atropine on the SA node
items.caption: The vagus nerve releases acetylcholine onto purple M2 receptors on the SA node and the heart slows; teal atropine blocks the receptors and the heart rate rises.

items.title: Central line, Seldinger technique
items.caption: Seldinger technique into the internal jugular vein: needle enters the vein, guidewire passes through it, needle removed, dilator, then catheter slides over the wire and the wire is removed.

items.title: Calcium homeostasis
items.caption: Low blood calcium triggers the parathyroid glands to release PTH, which acts on bone (calcium released), kidney (calcium kept, vitamin D activated) and gut (more calcium absorbed).

items.title: Gram positive and Gram negative walls
items.caption: Side-by-side cut-away of two bacterial walls: Gram positive with a thick peptidoglycan layer, Gram negative with a thin layer and an outer membrane; a purple stain sticks to the thick wall and washes out of the thin one.

items.title: Antibiotic targets
items.caption: One bacterium with four glowing target sites, each lit in turn: cell wall (penicillins), ribosome (macrolides), DNA (quinolones), folate pathway (trimethoprim).

items.title: RAAS and ACE inhibitors
items.caption: Low blood pressure makes the kidney release renin; angiotensinogen becomes angiotensin I, purple ACE in the lung makes angiotensin II, vessels narrow and aldosterone rises; teal ramipril blocks ACE.

items.title: Placental exchange
items.caption: Cut-away of the placenta: maternal blood pools around fetal villi; oxygen and glucose cross into fetal capillaries, carbon dioxide and waste cross back, and the bloods never mix.

items.title: Type 1 and type 2 diabetes
items.caption: Split screen: type 1, the pancreas makes almost no insulin; type 2, insulin arrives but the cell's receptors respond poorly and glucose stays outside the cell.

items.title: Iron and microcytic anaemia
items.caption: Iron is absorbed in the duodenum, carried by transferrin to the bone marrow and built into red cells; with too little iron the new red cells come out small and pale.

items.title: Burn depth
items.caption: A block of skin showing epidermis, dermis and fat; burns of increasing depth spread down layer by layer: superficial, partial thickness, full thickness.

items.title: Oxygen-haemoglobin dissociation curve
items.caption: A smooth S-shaped oxygen-haemoglobin curve drawn on dark navy; it slides to the right (labelled "Acidosis, fever, high CO2") and back to the left (labelled "Alkalosis, cold"), while a red cell beside it releases more or less oxygen.

items.title: CPR chest compressions
items.caption: Side cut-away of the chest: hands push the sternum down, the heart is squeezed and blood is pushed out to the brain, the chest recoils fully and the heart refills.

items.title: Fracture healing
items.caption: A broken long bone heals in stages: haematoma, soft callus, hard callus, remodelling back to normal shape.

items.title: Cardiac cycle
items.caption: A heart in cut-away going through one beat: atria contract, mitral and tricuspid valves close, ventricles squeeze, aortic and pulmonary valves open, then relax and refill.

items.title: Diuretic sites in the nephron
items.caption: A full nephron; each segment lights up in turn with the drug that acts there: proximal tubule (SGLT2 inhibitors), loop of Henle (furosemide), distal tubule (thiazides), collecting duct (spironolactone).

items.title: 5-alpha reductase inhibitors
items.caption: Testosterone is converted to DHT by 5-alpha reductase in the cell membrane; finasteride binds the enzyme and the conversion stops.

items.title: Beta-lactam action
items.caption: Penicillin-binding proteins cross-link the bacterial cell wall; penicillin binds them, cross-linking stops and the bacterium swells and bursts.

items.title: Beta-lactamase and clavulanate
items.caption: Beta-lactamase opens the penicillin ring; clavulanate binds the enzyme first and the penicillin passes through intact.

items.title: Loop diuretic
items.caption: In the thick ascending limb, NKCC2 moves sodium, potassium and chloride into the cell; furosemide blocks it and the ions stay in the urine.

items.title: Insulin and GLUT4
items.caption: Insulin binds its receptor on a muscle cell, GLUT4 vesicles fuse with the membrane and glucose flows into the cell.

items.title: Cardiac conduction and the ECG
items.caption: Depolarisation spreads from the SA node across the atria, pauses at the AV node and runs down the bundle branches, drawing the ECG in time.

items.title: Factor Xa inhibitor
items.caption: The clotting cascade converges on factor Xa and thrombin forms a fibrin mesh; apixaban binds factor Xa and the mesh stops forming.

items.title: Creating the pneumoperitoneum
items.caption: A Veress needle enters at the umbilicus, CO2 lifts the abdominal wall off the bowel, and a trocar enters safely into the space created.

items.title: Critical view of safety
items.caption: The hepatocystic triangle is cleared until only the cystic duct and cystic artery enter the gallbladder, with liver seen behind them.

items.title: Intussusception reduction
items.caption: A segment of ileum telescopes into the colon, then is squeezed back out from the distal end, never pulled.

items.title: Atherosclerosis
items.caption: Inside an artery wall: LDL enters, macrophages swallow it and become foam cells, a fatty plaque grows with a fibrous cap and narrows the lumen.

items.title: Plaque rupture in acute coronary syndrome
items.caption: A coronary plaque cap cracks, platelets rush in and a clot forms that blocks the artery, and the heart muscle beyond turns dark.

items.title: Atrial fibrillation
items.caption: Chaotic electrical wavelets swirl across the atria, only some pass the AV node, and the single ECG line at the bottom shows an irregular rhythm with no P waves (line only, no grid).

items.title: Ventricular tachycardia re-entry
items.caption: An electrical impulse circles endlessly around a scar in the ventricle wall, firing the ventricle rapidly, while the ECG line shows broad fast complexes (line only, no grid).

items.title: Adenosine in SVT
items.caption: An impulse loops through the AV node in a re-entry circuit causing fast SVT; teal adenosine briefly blocks the AV node, the loop breaks and normal rhythm returns.

items.title: Cardiac action potential and amiodarone
items.caption: A heart muscle cell action potential drawn as one line through phases 0 to 4, with purple sodium, calcium and potassium channels opening in time; teal amiodarone blocks potassium channels and the plateau lengthens.

items.title: Digoxin
items.caption: Teal digoxin blocks the purple sodium-potassium pump on a heart muscle cell, sodium builds up, more calcium stays in the cell and the cell contracts harder.

items.title: Beta blocker
items.caption: Adrenaline binds purple beta-1 receptors on the heart and it races; teal bisoprolol blocks the receptors and the heart slows and calms.

items.title: Heart failure
items.caption: A heart enlarges and pumps weakly, blood backs up into the lungs (fluid in alveoli) and into the legs (swollen ankles).

items.title: The synapse
items.caption: An impulse arrives at a nerve ending, vesicles release neurotransmitter into the gap, it binds purple receptors on the next neuron, then is taken back up.

items.title: SSRI
items.caption: Serotonin is released into a synapse and taken back by purple SERT transporters; teal sertraline blocks SERT and serotonin stays longer in the gap.

items.title: Benzodiazepine on GABA-A
items.caption: GABA binds a purple GABA-A receptor and chloride ions enter the neuron; teal diazepam binds a separate site and the channel opens more often, calming the neuron.

items.title: Seizure spread
items.caption: A burst of abnormal electrical firing starts in one area of the brain and spreads across both hemispheres; teal levetiracetam calms the firing back to normal.

items.title: Levodopa and carbidopa
items.caption: Dopamine neurons from the substantia nigra fade; teal levodopa with carbidopa crosses into the brain, becomes dopamine and the signal to the striatum returns.

items.title: Antipsychotic D2 blockade
items.caption: Excess dopamine in the mesolimbic pathway over-stimulates purple D2 receptors; teal haloperidol blocks them and the signal settles.

items.title: Warfarin and vitamin K
items.caption: In the liver, vitamin K is recycled by purple VKOR to activate factors II, VII, IX and X; teal warfarin blocks VKOR and the factors stay inactive.

items.title: Asthma and salbutamol
items.caption: An airway in cross-section narrows: smooth muscle tightens, the lining swells and mucus fills it; teal salbutamol relaxes the muscle and the airway reopens.

items.title: COPD
items.caption: Healthy alveoli with fine walls break down into large floppy air spaces (emphysema), and a bronchiole beside them fills with mucus (chronic bronchitis).

items.title: Pneumothorax and tension
items.caption: Air leaks from the lung into the pleural space and the lung collapses; in tension, the air keeps building and pushes the heart and trachea to the other side.

items.title: ARDS
items.caption: Alveoli flood with protein-rich fluid, a pink hyaline membrane lines the walls and oxygen cannot cross into the blood.

items.title: Pulmonary embolism
items.caption: A clot breaks off a deep vein in the leg, travels through the right heart and lodges in a pulmonary artery, and the lung tissue beyond it goes grey.

items.title: Airway manoeuvres
items.caption: Side view of the head: the tongue blocks the airway, then head tilt and chin lift (and then jaw thrust) lift the tongue forward and the airway opens.

items.title: Intubation
items.caption: Laryngoscope view: the blade lifts the epiglottis, the vocal cords come into view, and a tube passes between the cords into the trachea, its cuff inflating.

items.title: Raised intracranial pressure
items.caption: Inside the skull, brain, blood and CSF share fixed space; a growing mass first pushes out CSF and blood, then the brain is pushed down through the foramen magnum (herniation).

items.title: TB granuloma
items.caption: Inhaled TB bacilli are swallowed by macrophages, which gather with lymphocytes into a granuloma with a cheesy necrotic centre.

items.title: HIV life cycle and antiretrovirals
items.caption: HIV binds a CD4 cell, enters, reverse transcriptase copies its RNA into DNA, integrase puts it into the cell DNA, new viruses bud off; teal markers show where antiretrovirals block (reverse transcriptase, integrase, protease).

items.title: Malaria life cycle
items.caption: A mosquito injects sporozoites, they multiply in the liver, burst out and invade red cells, which rupture in cycles; teal artemether clears the parasites from red cells.

items.title: Macrolide
items.caption: A bacterial ribosome builds a protein chain; teal azithromycin binds the 50S subunit and the chain stops growing.

items.title: Aminoglycoside
items.caption: Teal gentamicin binds the 30S ribosome subunit, the ribosome misreads the code and faulty proteins are made.

items.title: Fluoroquinolone
items.caption: Purple DNA gyrase untwists bacterial DNA so it can copy; teal ciprofloxacin locks the enzyme and the DNA breaks.

items.title: Vancomycin
items.caption: Cell wall building blocks with D-Ala-D-Ala ends are being linked; teal vancomycin caps those ends and the wall cannot be built.

items.title: Metronidazole
items.caption: Teal metronidazole enters an anaerobic bacterium, is activated inside it and breaks its DNA strands.

items.title: Aciclovir
items.caption: In a herpes-infected cell, the virus's own thymidine kinase activates teal aciclovir, which is built into viral DNA and stops the chain.

items.title: Causes of acute kidney injury
items.caption: Three zones of one kidney diagram light up in turn: before the kidney (low blood flow), in the kidney (damaged tubules), after the kidney (blocked ureter).

items.title: Hyponatraemia and osmotic demyelination
items.caption: Low sodium in the blood makes water move into brain cells and they swell; then over-rapid correction pulls water out too fast and damages the myelin (osmotic demyelination).

items.title: Thiazide diuretic
items.caption: In the distal convoluted tubule, purple NCC transporters pull in amber sodium and chloride; teal indapamide blocks NCC and the ions stay in the urine.

items.title: SGLT2 inhibitor
items.caption: In the proximal tubule, purple SGLT2 transporters pull amber glucose back into the blood; teal empagliflozin blocks them and glucose passes out in the urine.

items.title: Metformin
items.caption: Teal metformin reduces glucose output from the liver and helps muscle take up glucose, and blood glucose falls.

items.title: Diabetic ketoacidosis
items.caption: With no insulin, glucose cannot enter cells, fat breaks down into ketones, the blood turns acidic and glucose spills into the urine with water.

items.title: Acute pancreatitis
items.caption: Pancreatic enzymes switch on inside the pancreas and begin digesting it, causing swelling and inflammation.

items.title: Gallstones
items.caption: A gallstone moves into the cystic duct and the gallbladder swells (biliary colic, cholecystitis), then a stone slips into the common bile duct and blocks bile flow.

items.title: Peptic ulcer and H. pylori
items.caption: H. pylori bacteria sit under the stomach mucus layer, weaken it and acid erodes the lining into an ulcer.

items.title: Appendicitis
items.caption: The appendix lumen is blocked, it swells with bacteria, the wall becomes inflamed and finally perforates.

items.title: Inguinal hernia, direct and indirect
items.caption: Groin cut-away: an indirect hernia goes through the deep ring along the inguinal canal; a direct hernia pushes straight through the weak back wall (Hesselbach's triangle).

items.title: Bowel obstruction
items.caption: A band blocks the small bowel; loops above it swell with gas and fluid while the bowel below collapses.

items.title: Compartment syndrome
items.caption: A leg cross-section with four muscle compartments; swelling in one raises its pressure, the veins are squashed, then the muscle turns pale; a fasciotomy opens the fascia and pressure falls.

items.title: Gout and allopurinol
items.caption: Needle-shaped urate crystals form in the big toe joint and cause inflammation; teal allopurinol blocks purple xanthine oxidase and uric acid production falls.

items.title: Methotrexate
items.caption: Purple DHFR enzyme recycles folate so cells can make DNA; teal methotrexate blocks DHFR and fast-dividing cells stop.

items.title: Oxytocin in post-partum haemorrhage
items.caption: After delivery, the uterus is soft and bleeding from the placental site; teal oxytocin makes the muscle contract and the criss-cross fibres squeeze the vessels shut.

items.title: Neonatal circulation at birth
items.caption: A fetal heart with the foramen ovale and ductus arteriosus open; at the first breath the lungs expand, the foramen ovale closes and the ductus constricts.

items.title: Wound healing
items.caption: A skin wound heals in stages: clot (haemostasis), white cells (inflammation), new tissue and vessels (proliferation), scar (remodelling).

items.title: IV cannulation
items.caption: A cannula enters a vein, blood appears in the flashback chamber, the plastic cannula slides off the needle into the vein and the needle withdraws.

items.title: Lumbar puncture
items.caption: Side view of the lower spine: the needle passes between the spinous processes through ligaments and dura into the CSF space below the end of the spinal cord.

items.title: Chest drain insertion
items.caption: Side chest view: the safe triangle is outlined, the drain passes over the top of the rib into the pleural space, and air bubbles out through an underwater seal.

items.title: Nerve action potential
items.caption: A nerve impulse travels along a myelinated axon, jumping from node to node as sodium rushes in and potassium flows out.

items.title: Propofol
items.caption: Teal propofol enhances purple GABA-A receptors across the brain, neurons quieten and the brain activity fades into anaesthesia.

items.title: Ondansetron
items.caption: Serotonin from the gut lining stimulates purple 5-HT3 receptors on the vagus nerve and in the brain's vomiting centre; teal ondansetron blocks them.

items.title: GLP-1 agonist
items.caption: Teal semaglutide binds purple GLP-1 receptors: the pancreas releases more insulin, the stomach empties slower and the brain feels full.

items.title: Inhaler technique and spacer
items.caption: A metered-dose inhaler puffs medicine: without a spacer most of it hits the throat; with a spacer and a slow breath the particles reach deep into the airways.

items.title: Dengue plasma leakage
items.caption: Dengue virus damages the lining of small vessels, plasma leaks out into the tissues, the blood thickens and the platelet count falls.

items.title: Virus replication
items.caption: A virus attaches to a cell, enters, releases its genome, the cell makes copies of the virus and new viruses burst out.

items.title: Acid-base balance
items.caption: A balance scale with bicarbonate on one side and carbon dioxide on the other; when acid is added the lungs breathe off more CO2 to rebalance.

items.title: Pre-eclampsia
items.caption: In normal pregnancy the spiral arteries widen into wide channels; in pre-eclampsia they stay narrow, the placenta is starved and releases factors that raise the mother's blood pressure.

items.title: Bisphosphonate
items.caption: Purple osteoclasts dissolve bone surface; teal alendronate sticks to the bone, the osteoclasts take it up and stop resorbing.

items.title: Post-partum haemorrhage, the 4 Ts
items.caption: A uterus after birth with four panels lighting up: Tone (soft uterus), Trauma (tear), Tissue (retained placenta), Thrombin (clotting problem).

items.title: Azole antifungal
items.caption: A fungal cell makes ergosterol for its membrane using purple 14-alpha demethylase; teal fluconazole blocks the enzyme and the membrane weakens.

items.title: Sickle cell vaso-occlusion
items.caption: Red cells turn into sickle shapes when oxygen is low, stick together and block a small vessel, and the tissue beyond goes dark.

items.title: Bilirubin and jaundice
items.caption: Old red cells break down to bilirubin, the liver conjugates it and excretes it in bile; when the flow is blocked, bilirubin backs up and the skin turns yellow.

items.title: CSF flow, hydrocephalus and VP shunt
items.caption: CSF is made in the ventricles, flows through the aqueduct and is absorbed over the brain; when blocked the ventricles swell, and a VP shunt drains CSF to the abdomen.

items.title: Frank-Starling law
items.caption: A heart fills with more blood, the muscle fibres stretch and it pumps out more; a curve beside it rises then flattens.

items.title: Alveolar gas exchange
items.caption: An alveolus with a capillary wrapped around it: oxygen crosses into red cells and carbon dioxide crosses into the alveolus with every breath.

items.title: Ventilation-perfusion mismatch
items.caption: Three alveolus-capillary pairs: normal, shunt (blood flows past a flooded alveolus), dead space (air reaches an alveolus with no blood flow).

items.title: Labour
items.caption: Front view of the pelvis: the cervix thins and opens while the baby's head descends and rotates through the pelvis.

items.title: Ectopic pregnancy
items.caption: A fertilised egg travels down the fallopian tube but implants in the tube wall instead of the uterus, the tube swells and bleeds.

items.title: Menstrual cycle
items.caption: FSH and LH rise and fall over 28 days as a follicle grows, ovulates and becomes the corpus luteum, while the uterine lining thickens and sheds.

items.title: Osteoarthritis and rheumatoid arthritis
items.caption: Two knee joints side by side: osteoarthritis with worn cartilage and bone spurs; rheumatoid arthritis with a thick inflamed synovium eroding the bone.

items.title: Renal colic
items.caption: A kidney stone moves down the ureter, the ureter spasms behind it, and it passes into the bladder.

items.title: Diabetic retinopathy
items.caption: A retina view progresses: tiny dot haemorrhages and microaneurysms, then cotton wool spots, then fragile new vessels growing (proliferative).

items.title: Glaucoma
items.caption: Aqueous humour flows from the ciliary body through the pupil and drains at the angle; when the drain is blocked, pressure rises and presses on the optic nerve.

items.title: Cataract
items.caption: A clear lens slowly clouds over and light scatters; in surgery the cloudy lens is removed and a clear artificial lens is placed.

items.title: BPPV and the Epley manoeuvre
items.caption: Loose crystals sit in the posterior semicircular canal; the Epley head turns roll them round the canal and out into the utricle.

items.title: Myasthenia gravis
items.caption: Antibodies block purple acetylcholine receptors at the neuromuscular junction, fewer receptors fire and the muscle tires; teal pyridostigmine lets more acetylcholine reach the remaining receptors.

items.title: Guillain-Barre syndrome
items.caption: Antibodies attack the myelin around peripheral nerves, the myelin peels away and the nerve signal slows from the feet upward.

items.title: Subarachnoid haemorrhage
items.caption: A berry aneurysm at the circle of Willis swells and bursts, blood spreads through the subarachnoid space around the brain.

items.title: Extradural and subdural haematoma
items.caption: Two skull cut-aways side by side: extradural (lens-shaped bleed from the middle meningeal artery between skull and dura) and subdural (crescent bleed from bridging veins under the dura).

items.title: Spinal and epidural
items.caption: Cross-section of the spine: an epidural needle stops in the epidural space; a spinal needle goes through the dura into the CSF.

items.title: Primary haemostasis
items.caption: A vessel wall is cut, platelets stick to exposed collagen with von Willebrand factor, activate and form a plug, then fibrin strands reinforce it.

items.title: DIC
items.caption: Many tiny clots form throughout small vessels, using up platelets and clotting factors, and bleeding starts at the same time.

items.title: ABO transfusion reaction
items.caption: Group A red cells meet anti-B and nothing happens; group B cells meet anti-B antibodies and clump together.

items.title: Nephrotic and nephritic
items.caption: Two glomeruli side by side: nephrotic with protein leaking through the filter; nephritic with inflamed walls leaking red cells.

items.title: Hypoglycaemia
items.caption: Blood glucose drops, the brain runs short of fuel and glucagon from the pancreas makes the liver release glucose; teal IV dextrose restores it.

items.title: Magnesium sulfate in eclampsia
items.caption: Over-excited brain neurons fire in a seizure; teal magnesium sulfate calms the neurons and relaxes the vessel walls.

items.title: Lung cancer spread
items.caption: A tumour grows in the bronchus, spreads to the hilar lymph nodes and then to bone, liver and brain.

items.title: Adenoma to carcinoma sequence
items.caption: Normal colon lining grows into a small polyp, a larger adenoma, then a cancer invading the wall.

items.title: Breast lymphatics and sentinel node
items.caption: Breast tissue with a tumour; lymph drains to the axillary nodes and a blue dye marks the sentinel node first.

items.title: P2Y12 inhibitor (clopidogrel)
items.caption: ADP binds P2Y12 receptors on small disc-shaped platelets, which swell, put out spikes and stick together; clopidogrel occupies the receptors and the platelets stay smooth and separate.

items.title: Urinary catheterisation
items.caption: Side cut-away of the male pelvis: the catheter passes along the urethra and through the prostate until its tip lies inside the bladder; only then is the balloon inflated, sitting against the bladder neck, and urine drains.

items.title: Liver fibrosis to cirrhosis
items.caption: A healthy smooth liver gradually becomes smaller, shrunken and knobbly with pale scar bands and regenerative nodules; an inset shows liver cells being replaced by scar.

items.title: Hyperkalaemia on the ECG
items.caption: As potassium rises the ECG shows peaked T waves, then flat P waves, then a wide QRS and a sine wave; after calcium gluconate and insulin with glucose the trace returns to a normal ECG.

items.title: Glomerular filtration
items.caption: Blood enters the glomerular capillary tuft and a clear pale yellow filtrate passes into Bowman's capsule and on to the tubule, while red cells and large proteins stay in the blood.

items.title: Angiotensin receptor blocker (losartan)
items.caption: Angiotensin II binds AT1 receptors on the artery wall and the artery narrows; losartan then fills the receptors and the artery opens wide again.

items.title: Nasogastric tube placement
items.caption: A nasogastric tube passes through the nose, down the back of the throat and the oesophagus until its tip lies in the stomach; aspirate with a pH below 5.5 confirms the position.

items.title: Variceal band ligation
items.caption: Inside the oesophagus a swollen varix is sucked into the endoscope cap, a rubber band snaps around its base and the strangled varix darkens and shrinks.

items.title: ACE inhibitor and bradykinin cough
items.caption: ACE breaks down bradykinin; ramipril blocks ACE, bradykinin builds up in the airway lining and triggers a dry cough.

items.title: Calcium channel blocker (amlodipine)
items.caption: Calcium ions enter an artery's smooth muscle through L-type channels and it contracts; amlodipine blocks the channels and the artery relaxes and widens.

items.title: Verapamil on the AV node
items.caption: Electrical impulses pass quickly through the AV node; verapamil blocks calcium channels in the node and fewer impulses get through, the heart rate slows.

items.title: Ivabradine on the SA node
items.caption: The SA node fires using the funny current through If channels; ivabradine blocks them and the node fires more slowly.

items.title: Sacubitril with valsartan
items.caption: Natriuretic peptides are broken down by neprilysin; sacubitril blocks neprilysin so peptides rise and widen vessels, while valsartan blocks AT1.

items.title: Hydralazine
items.caption: Hydralazine acts on artery muscle and the arteries widen, lowering blood pressure, while the veins stay unchanged.

items.title: Clonidine (central alpha-2 agonist)
items.caption: Clonidine activates alpha-2 receptors in the brainstem, sympathetic signals to the heart and vessels fall and blood pressure drops.

items.title: Dobutamine on beta-1
items.caption: Dobutamine binds beta-1 receptors on heart muscle and the heart contracts more strongly with each beat.

items.title: Vasopressin on V1 and V2
items.caption: Vasopressin binds V1 receptors on arteries (they narrow) and V2 receptors in the collecting duct (water channels move to the surface and water is reabsorbed).

items.title: Mannitol in raised ICP
items.caption: Mannitol in the blood draws water out of the swollen brain across the blood-brain barrier, the brain shrinks back and pressure falls.

items.title: Tranexamic acid
items.caption: Plasmin breaks a fibrin clot apart; tranexamic acid blocks plasminogen from binding fibrin and the clot stays intact.

items.title: Dabigatran (direct thrombin inhibitor)
items.caption: Thrombin turns fibrinogen into fibrin strands; dabigatran binds thrombin directly and fibrin stops forming.

items.title: Protamine reversal of heparin
items.caption: Heparin molecules are bound to antithrombin; positively charged protamine binds heparin and pulls it away, clotting returns.

items.title: Reversing warfarin
items.caption: After warfarin, clotting factors II, VII, IX, X are low; vitamin K lets the liver make them again and prothrombin complex concentrate replaces them at once.

items.title: Fibrinolysis in myocardial infarction
items.caption: A clot blocks a coronary artery; tenecteplase turns plasminogen into plasmin, the clot dissolves and blood reaches the heart muscle again.

items.title: Glycoprotein IIb/IIIa inhibitor
items.caption: Activated platelets join together through fibrinogen bridges between GP IIb/IIIa receptors; tirofiban blocks the receptors and the bridges cannot form.

items.title: Ezetimibe
items.caption: Cholesterol from food enters gut cells through NPC1L1 transporters; ezetimibe blocks them and less cholesterol is absorbed.

items.title: PCSK9 inhibitor
items.caption: PCSK9 makes liver LDL receptors get destroyed; a antibody binds PCSK9, receptors return to the surface and pull LDL out of the blood.

items.title: Fibrates on PPAR-alpha
items.caption: Fenofibrate activates PPAR-alpha in liver cells, lipoprotein lipase rises and triglyceride particles are cleared from blood.

items.title: DPP-4 inhibitor
items.caption: GLP-1 from the gut is quickly broken down by DPP-4; sitagliptin blocks DPP-4 so GLP-1 lasts longer and insulin rises after meals.

items.title: Pioglitazone
items.caption: Pioglitazone activates PPAR-gamma in fat cells, more GLUT4 transporters appear and glucose enters cells.

items.title: Insulin types and their timing
items.caption: A time graph shows rapid-acting, short-acting, intermediate and long-acting insulin curves rising and falling over 24 hours, drawn one after another.

items.title: Adrenal crisis and hydrocortisone
items.caption: The adrenal glands fail, cortisol falls and blood pressure and glucose drop; hydrocortisone injection restores them.

items.title: Fludrocortisone on the kidney
items.caption: Fludrocortisone acts like aldosterone in the collecting duct: sodium is kept and potassium is lost into the urine.

items.title: Desmopressin in diabetes insipidus
items.caption: Without ADH water pours out as dilute urine; desmopressin binds V2 receptors, aquaporin channels open and urine becomes concentrated.

items.title: Dopamine agonist and prolactin
items.caption: A pituitary tumour releases too much prolactin; cabergoline activates D2 receptors and prolactin release falls, the tumour shrinks.

items.title: Octreotide
items.caption: Octreotide acts like somatostatin, binds receptors on gut and pituitary cells and switches off hormone release and gut blood flow.

items.title: Denosumab
items.caption: RANKL binds RANK on osteoclast precursors and they mature; a antibody binds RANKL and osteoclasts stop forming.

items.title: Hormone replacement therapy
items.caption: After menopause oestrogen falls, bone thins and hot flushes start; oestrogen replacement protects bone and settles the flushes.

items.title: Combined oral contraceptive
items.caption: Oestrogen and progestogen suppress FSH and LH from the pituitary, the follicle does not ripen and no egg is released.

items.title: Levonorgestrel emergency pill
items.caption: Levonorgestrel delays the LH surge so the follicle does not release an egg.

items.title: Tamoxifen
items.caption: Oestrogen binds receptors on breast cancer cells and they grow; tamoxifen occupies the oestrogen receptor and growth stops.

items.title: Aromatase inhibitor
items.caption: In fat tissue aromatase turns androgens into oestrogen; letrozole blocks aromatase and oestrogen falls.

items.title: GnRH analogue in prostate cancer
items.caption: Leuprorelin first causes a testosterone flare, then switches off the pituitary so testosterone falls and the prostate cancer shrinks.

items.title: PDE5 inhibitor
items.caption: Nitric oxide raises cGMP in smooth muscle and vessels relax; PDE5 breaks cGMP down; sildenafil blocks PDE5 and relaxation lasts.

items.title: Mifepristone and misoprostol
items.caption: Mifepristone blocks progesterone receptors in the uterus lining; then misoprostol makes the uterus contract and the cervix soften.

items.title: Nifedipine as a tocolytic
items.caption: Uterine muscle contracts with calcium entry; nifedipine blocks calcium channels and the contractions slow.

items.title: Antenatal corticosteroids
items.caption: Dexamethasone crosses the placenta, the baby's lungs make surfactant and the alveoli stay open at birth.

items.title: H2 receptor blocker
items.caption: Histamine binds H2 receptors on the parietal cell and acid pours out; famotidine blocks H2 and acid falls.

items.title: Alginate antacid
items.caption: Alginate forms a raft floating on top of stomach contents and stops acid rising into the oesophagus.

items.title: Metoclopramide
items.caption: Metoclopramide blocks D2 receptors in the vomiting centre and speeds stomach emptying into the duodenum.

items.title: Loperamide
items.caption: Loperamide binds opioid receptors in the gut wall, peristalsis slows and more water is absorbed.

items.title: How laxatives work
items.caption: Three panels: bulk fibre swells the stool, osmotic lactulose draws water into the bowel, a stimulant senna makes the bowel contract.

items.title: Lactulose in hepatic encephalopathy
items.caption: Lactulose acidifies the colon, ammonia is trapped as ammonium and passed in stool, and the brain clears.

items.title: Mesalazine in ulcerative colitis
items.caption: Mesalazine is released in the colon and calms the inflamed lining, which heals.

items.title: Anti-TNF biologic
items.caption: TNF-alpha drives inflammation in joints and gut; a antibody (infliximab) binds TNF-alpha and the inflammation settles.

items.title: Azathioprine
items.caption: Azathioprine is turned into a false purine and blocks DNA building in dividing lymphocytes, which stop multiplying.

items.title: Calcineurin inhibitor
items.caption: T-cell activation needs calcineurin to switch on IL-2; tacrolimus blocks calcineurin and the T cell stays quiet.

items.title: Hydroxychloroquine
items.caption: Hydroxychloroquine raises the pH inside immune cell vesicles and toll-like receptor signalling falls, calming autoimmunity.

items.title: Colchicine
items.caption: Colchicine binds tubulin, white cell microtubules cannot form and neutrophils cannot move into the inflamed gout joint.

items.title: Febuxostat vs uric acid
items.caption: Purine breakdown makes uric acid through xanthine oxidase; febuxostat blocks the enzyme and uric acid crystals dissolve.

items.title: Rituximab
items.caption: A antibody binds CD20 on B cells and they are destroyed by complement and immune cells.

items.title: Immune checkpoint inhibitor
items.caption: A tumour cell uses PD-L1 to switch off a T cell; a antibody blocks PD-1 and the T cell attacks the tumour.

items.title: Trastuzumab
items.caption: HER2 receptors crowd a breast cancer cell and drive growth; trastuzumab binds HER2 and growth signals stop.

items.title: Imatinib
items.caption: The BCR-ABL kinase drives white cell growth in CML; imatinib sits in its ATP pocket and the signal stops.

items.title: Platinum chemotherapy
items.caption: Cisplatin crosslinks the DNA strands of a cancer cell, the DNA cannot be copied and the cell dies.

items.title: Vinca alkaloid
items.caption: Vincristine binds tubulin, the spindle cannot form and the dividing cell stops in mitosis.

items.title: Doxorubicin
items.caption: Doxorubicin slips between DNA bases and blocks topoisomerase II; a side panel shows heart muscle damage.

items.title: 5-Fluorouracil
items.caption: 5-FU blocks thymidylate synthase so the cell runs out of thymidine and cannot make DNA.

items.title: Folinic acid rescue
items.caption: Methotrexate blocks DHFR and normal cells starve of folate; folinic acid bypasses the block and normal cells recover.

items.title: Hydroxyurea in sickle cell
items.caption: Hydroxyurea makes red cells produce more fetal haemoglobin, which stops sickling.

items.title: Iron chelation
items.caption: Excess iron deposits in heart and liver; deferasirox grabs the iron and it leaves in stool.

items.title: Erythropoietin
items.caption: The kidney makes erythropoietin which tells the bone marrow to make red cells; in kidney failure epoetin replaces it.

items.title: Vitamin B12 and folate in red cell making
items.caption: Large immature red cells in the marrow fail to divide without B12 and folate; B12 and folate replacement and normal cells form.

items.title: Intravenous iron
items.caption: Iron enters the blood, is carried by transferrin to the marrow and new red cells fill with haemoglobin.

items.title: Penicillin allergy reaction
items.caption: Penicillin binds IgE on mast cells, the mast cells burst and release histamine; hives and airway swelling appear.

items.title: Trauma primary survey
items.caption: A trauma patient outline with each step lighting up in order: airway with neck protection, breathing, circulation with bleeding control, disability, exposure.

items.title: Massive transfusion
items.caption: Red cells, plasma and platelets given together in balance to a bleeding patient while bleeding is controlled.

items.title: Tourniquet for limb bleeding
items.caption: A band is placed above a bleeding limb wound and tightened until the arterial bleeding stops.

items.title: Pelvic binder
items.caption: An open-book pelvic fracture is closed by a binder placed over the greater trochanters, reducing bleeding.

items.title: FAST ultrasound
items.caption: An ultrasound probe checks four windows in turn: around the liver, around the spleen, the pelvis and the heart, and finds dark fluid.

items.title: Cervical spine immobilisation
items.caption: The neck is held still in line while the patient is moved as one unit, protecting the spinal cord.

items.title: Flail chest
items.caption: Several ribs are broken in two places, the segment moves in when breathing in and out when breathing out.

items.title: Haemothorax
items.caption: Blood collects in the pleural space and compresses the lung; a chest drain removes it.

items.title: Needle decompression
items.caption: In tension pneumothorax a needle in the 2nd intercostal space or 5th space releases trapped air and the heart and lung return to place.

items.title: Splenic injury
items.caption: A blow to the left upper abdomen tears the spleen and blood fills the abdomen.

items.title: Liver injury and packing
items.caption: The liver is torn and bleeds; surgical packs press on it and bleeding slows.

items.title: Damage control surgery
items.caption: Stop bleeding and leaks quickly, close temporarily, warm and resuscitate in ICU, then come back for the final repair.

items.title: Rule of nines
items.caption: Body areas light up with their burn percentages: head 9, each arm 9, front 18, back 18, each leg 18, perineum 1.

items.title: Burns fluid resuscitation
items.caption: Fluid leaks from vessels after a burn; IV fluid replaces it, half in the first 8 hours.

items.title: Inhalation injury
items.caption: Hot smoke burns the upper airway, swelling starts to close it, early intubation keeps it open.

items.title: Split skin graft
items.caption: A thin layer of skin is taken by a dermatome, meshed, spread over a wound and new vessels grow in.

items.title: Local flap
items.caption: A nearby flap of skin is rotated into a defect, keeping its own blood supply.

items.title: Simple interrupted suturing
items.caption: A needle passes through skin edges at the same depth on both sides and the knot brings the edges together.

items.title: Layered wound closure
items.caption: A deep wound is closed layer by layer: muscle, fat, then skin.

items.title: Surgical site infection
items.caption: Bacteria enter a wound, it becomes red and pus forms; opening and draining it lets it heal.

items.title: Abscess formation and drainage
items.caption: Bacteria trigger white cells, a pus pocket forms with a wall; an incision drains it.

items.title: Laparoscopic port placement
items.caption: The abdomen is inflated with gas, a camera port goes in at the umbilicus and working ports are placed under vision.

items.title: Diathermy
items.caption: Monopolar: current flows from the tip through the body to a pad; bipolar: current flows only between the two forceps tips.

items.title: Ileostomy and colostomy
items.caption: Bowel is brought through the abdominal wall and opened as a stoma into a bag.

items.title: Bowel anastomosis
items.caption: Two cut bowel ends are joined with a stapler and blood flow is checked.

items.title: Anastomotic leak
items.caption: Bowel contents leak through a gap at the join, causing peritonitis.

items.title: Peritonitis
items.caption: A perforated organ spills its content, the peritoneum becomes inflamed and the abdomen becomes rigid.

items.title: Perforated duodenal ulcer
items.caption: An ulcer erodes through the duodenal wall, air and acid escape and air appears under the diaphragm.

items.title: Sigmoid volvulus
items.caption: The sigmoid colon twists on its mesentery, the bowel swells and a flatus tube untwists it.

items.title: Acute mesenteric ischaemia
items.caption: A clot blocks the superior mesenteric artery and the small bowel turns dark.

items.title: Abdominal hernias
items.caption: Bulges at the groin, femoral canal, umbilicus and an old scar, each with its own neck.

items.title: Strangulated hernia
items.caption: Bowel trapped in a tight hernia neck swells, its blood supply is cut and it turns dark.

items.title: Mesh hernia repair
items.caption: A mesh is laid over the weak area of the inguinal floor and fixed, reinforcing it.

items.title: Haemorrhoids
items.caption: Swollen vascular cushions in the anal canal bleed or slip out; rubber band ligation cuts their supply.

items.title: Anal fissure
items.caption: A tear in the anal lining, sphincter spasm keeps it from healing; relaxing the sphincter lets it heal.

items.title: Anal fistula
items.caption: An anal gland abscess bursts out through the skin making a tract; a seton is passed through.

items.title: Pilonidal sinus
items.caption: Hairs drill into the skin of the natal cleft forming sinuses and an abscess.

items.title: Colorectal cancer staging
items.caption: The tumour grows through the bowel wall layers, then into nodes, then to the liver.

items.title: Gastric cancer
items.caption: A tumour grows in the stomach wall and spreads to nearby nodes.

items.title: Oesophageal cancer
items.caption: A tumour narrows the oesophagus, food sticks above it.

items.title: Pancreatic head cancer
items.caption: A tumour in the pancreatic head blocks the bile duct, jaundice follows and the gallbladder swells.

items.title: Bariatric surgery
items.caption: Sleeve gastrectomy makes the stomach a narrow tube; gastric bypass makes a small pouch joined to lower bowel.

items.title: Nissen fundoplication
items.caption: The top of the stomach is wrapped around the lower oesophagus to stop reflux.

items.title: Thyroidectomy and the recurrent laryngeal nerve
items.caption: The thyroid is removed while the recurrent laryngeal nerve and parathyroids are kept safe.

items.title: Breast cancer surgery choices
items.caption: A wide local excision removes the lump with a margin; a mastectomy removes the whole breast.

items.title: Carotid endarterectomy
items.caption: The carotid artery is opened and the plaque peeled out, then closed with a patch.

items.title: Endovascular aneurysm repair
items.caption: A stent graft is passed up from the groin and opens inside the aneurysm, sealing it off.

items.title: Acute limb ischaemia
items.caption: A clot suddenly blocks the leg artery: pale, pulseless, painful, cold; an embolectomy catheter pulls it out.

items.title: Amputation levels
items.caption: Leg outlines showing below-knee and above-knee levels and the healed stump.

items.title: AV fistula for dialysis
items.caption: An artery is joined to a vein at the wrist, the vein grows large and strong enough for dialysis needles.

items.title: Kidney stone treatments
items.caption: Shock waves break a stone from outside, a ureteroscope lasers a ureter stone and PCNL removes a large stone through the back.

items.title: Ureteric stent
items.caption: A soft tube coils in the kidney at one end and in the bladder at the other, letting urine pass a blockage.

items.title: Transurethral resection of prostate
items.caption: A scope in the urethra trims the enlarged prostate and the channel opens.

items.title: Testicular torsion
items.caption: The testis twists on its cord, blood is cut off; untwisting and fixing restores flow.

items.title: Hydrocele
items.caption: Fluid collects around the testis in the tunica vaginalis; light shines through it.

items.title: Bladder cancer
items.caption: A tumour on the bladder wall is removed by a scope through the urethra.

items.title: Fracture patterns
items.caption: Bone shown breaking in different patterns: transverse, oblique, spiral, comminuted, greenstick.

items.title: Fracture fixation methods
items.caption: A cast, a plate with screws, an intramedullary nail and an external fixator holding a broken bone.

items.title: Total hip replacement
items.caption: The femoral head and socket are replaced by a metal stem with a ball and a cup.

items.title: Total knee replacement
items.caption: Worn knee surfaces are replaced by metal caps with a plastic spacer.

items.title: ACL tear and reconstruction
items.caption: The ACL tears in a twist; a graft is passed through bone tunnels to replace it.

items.title: Meniscus tear
items.caption: The meniscus cushions the knee; a tear catches and the knee locks.

items.title: Shoulder dislocation and reduction
items.caption: The humeral head slips forward out of the socket and is guided back in.

items.title: Rotator cuff tear
items.caption: The supraspinatus tendon frays and tears under the acromion.

items.title: Distal radius fracture
items.caption: A fall on the outstretched hand bends the wrist bone back; it is reduced and held.

items.title: Scaphoid fracture
items.caption: The scaphoid breaks across its waist and its blood supply from the far end is cut.

items.title: Carpal tunnel syndrome
items.caption: The median nerve is squeezed under the ligament in the wrist; cutting the ligament frees it.

items.title: Tendon repair
items.caption: A cut flexor tendon is stitched end to end and glides again.

items.title: Osteomyelitis
items.caption: Bacteria settle in bone, pus builds, dead bone forms and new bone grows around it.

items.title: Septic arthritis
items.caption: Bacteria enter a joint, pus fills it and cartilage is damaged; it is washed out.

items.title: Lumbar disc prolapse
items.caption: The disc centre bulges out and presses on a nerve root, pain runs down the leg.

items.title: Cauda equina syndrome
items.caption: A large central disc presses on all nerve roots below the cord, bladder and saddle area are affected.

items.title: Spinal stenosis
items.caption: Thickened ligament, disc and joints narrow the canal, walking squeezes the nerves.

items.title: Spinal cord injury levels
items.caption: Cord damage at neck, chest and lower levels shown with the parts of the body affected.

items.title: Plaster and swelling
items.caption: A cast on a swollen limb, the limb swells more and the cast is split to release pressure.

items.title: DVT prevention after surgery
items.caption: Calf pumps, stockings and low molecular weight heparin keep blood moving in leg veins.

items.title: Pre-operative fasting
items.caption: A clock shows food stopped 6 hours and clear fluids 2 hours before anaesthesia, the stomach empty.

items.title: Airway assessment
items.caption: Mouth opening, Mallampati view, neck movement and jaw are checked to predict a hard intubation.

items.title: Supraglottic airway
items.caption: A laryngeal mask sits over the larynx and seals around it so the patient can be ventilated.

items.title: Rapid sequence induction
items.caption: Oxygen first, then induction drug and fast-acting relaxant, cricoid support and the tube placed quickly.

items.title: Emergency front of neck access
items.caption: A cut through the cricothyroid membrane and a tube passed into the trachea when intubation fails.

items.title: Capnography
items.caption: The CO2 waveform appears with each breath when the tube is in the trachea and stays flat if it is in the oesophagus.

items.title: Peripheral nerve block
items.caption: An ultrasound shows the needle reaching a nerve and the local anaesthetic spreading around it.

items.title: Tracheostomy
items.caption: A tube is placed through the front of the neck into the trachea and its cuff is inflated.

items.title: Arterial line
items.caption: A cannula in the radial artery connects to a transducer and a pressure waveform shows.

items.title: Abdominal paracentesis
items.caption: A needle drains fluid from the lower abdomen, away from the vessels.

items.title: Pleural tap
items.caption: A needle passes above the rib into the pleural fluid and drains it.

items.title: Intraosseous access
items.caption: A needle drills into the shin bone marrow and fluids flow into the circulation.

items.title: Synchronised cardioversion
items.caption: The shock is timed on the R wave to restore sinus rhythm.

items.title: Fasciotomy
items.caption: The tight muscle compartments of the leg are opened through two long cuts and the muscle swells out freely.

items.title: Escharotomy
items.caption: A tight burn eschar around the chest is cut and the chest can expand again.

items.title: Source control in sepsis
items.caption: Drain the abscess, remove the infected device or bowel, and antibiotics start working.

items.title: Enhanced recovery after surgery
items.caption: Before, during and after surgery: carbohydrate drink, careful fluids, early eating and walking.

items.title: Coronary artery bypass graft
items.caption: A vein from the leg and the internal mammary artery are joined beyond the coronary blockages and blood flows around them.

items.title: Craniotomy for extradural haematoma
items.caption: A bone flap is lifted, the clot between skull and dura is sucked out and the bleeding artery sealed.

items.title: Burr hole for chronic subdural
items.caption: A small hole in the skull lets the old liquid subdural blood drain and the brain re-expands.

items.title: Fertilisation and implantation
items.caption: Sperm meets the egg in the fallopian tube, the embryo divides as it travels and implants in the uterine lining.

items.title: hCG in early pregnancy
items.caption: The placenta makes hCG, which keeps the corpus luteum making progesterone; a pregnancy test detects it.

items.title: Gestational diabetes
items.caption: Placental hormones raise insulin resistance, maternal glucose crosses the placenta and the baby grows large.

items.title: Placenta praevia
items.caption: The placenta lies low and covers the cervix; bleeding happens as the cervix starts to open.

items.title: Placental abruption
items.caption: The placenta separates early from the uterine wall and blood collects behind it.

items.title: CTG basics
items.caption: A fetal heart trace with baseline rate, variability and accelerations, then a late deceleration after each contraction.

items.title: Umbilical cord prolapse
items.caption: The cord slips down before the baby; the presenting part is lifted off it and the mother goes knees to chest.

items.title: Shoulder dystocia
items.caption: The baby's shoulder catches behind the pubic bone; legs pulled back and pressure above the pubis free it.

items.title: Breech presentation
items.caption: The baby is bottom down; external cephalic version turns it head down.

items.title: Caesarean section
items.caption: Layers are opened to the lower uterine segment, the baby is delivered and the uterus closed.

items.title: Perineal tears
items.caption: Degrees of tear from skin only to involving the anal sphincter.

items.title: Rhesus disease and anti-D
items.caption: Rh positive baby cells enter an Rh negative mother, antibodies form and attack the next baby; anti-D prevents this.

items.title: Twin pregnancy
items.caption: Identical twins from one egg sharing a placenta, non-identical twins from two eggs with two placentas.

items.title: Miscarriage types
items.caption: Threatened (cervix closed, pregnancy continues), inevitable (cervix open), complete (uterus empty).

items.title: Molar pregnancy
items.caption: Abnormal placental tissue grows as clusters of vesicles and hCG rises very high.

items.title: Ovarian follicle and ovulation
items.caption: FSH grows follicles, one dominates, the LH surge releases the egg and the corpus luteum forms.

items.title: Polycystic ovary syndrome
items.caption: Many small follicles stop growing, androgens rise and ovulation stops.

items.title: Endometriosis
items.caption: Lining tissue grows outside the uterus on ovaries and pelvis, bleeds monthly and causes scarring.

items.title: Uterine fibroids
items.caption: Benign muscle lumps grow inside, within and on the outside of the uterine wall.

items.title: Ovarian torsion
items.caption: An enlarged ovary twists on its pedicle and its blood supply is cut off.

items.title: Cervical screening and HPV
items.caption: HPV infects the cervix transformation zone, cells change and screening finds them early.

items.title: Cervical cancer progression
items.caption: Abnormal cells become CIN, then invasive cancer spreads into the surrounding tissue.

items.title: Ovarian cancer spread
items.caption: A tumour on the ovary sheds cells across the peritoneum and fluid collects.

items.title: Menopause
items.caption: Follicles run out, oestrogen falls and FSH rises, periods stop.

items.title: Intrauterine device
items.caption: A T-shaped device sits in the uterus; copper is toxic to sperm, the hormonal type thickens the cervical mucus.

items.title: Pelvic inflammatory disease
items.caption: Infection rises from the cervix into the uterus and tubes, the tubes scar and can block.

items.title: Uterine prolapse
items.caption: Weak pelvic floor lets the uterus descend into the vagina.

items.title: Newborn resuscitation
items.caption: Dry and warm the baby, open the airway, give 5 inflation breaths, check heart rate, then chest compressions if needed.

items.title: Apgar score
items.caption: Five signs scored at 1 and 5 minutes: heart rate, breathing, tone, reflex, colour.

items.title: Neonatal jaundice and phototherapy
items.caption: Bilirubin builds in a newborn's skin; blue light turns it into a form the baby can pass.

items.title: Respiratory distress in preterm babies
items.caption: Without surfactant preterm alveoli collapse; surfactant given down the tube opens them.

items.title: Necrotising enterocolitis
items.caption: In a preterm gut bacteria invade the bowel wall, gas forms in the wall and the bowel can perforate.

items.title: Pyloric stenosis
items.caption: The pylorus muscle thickens, milk cannot pass and is vomited; the muscle is split and food passes.

items.title: Malrotation and volvulus
items.caption: The gut does not rotate properly and twists, cutting blood supply; it is untwisted.

items.title: Hirschsprung disease
items.caption: Nerve cells are missing in the last part of the bowel, it stays tight and the bowel above swells.

items.title: Ventricular septal defect
items.caption: Blood passes left to right through a hole between the ventricles and the lungs get extra blood.

items.title: Tetralogy of Fallot
items.caption: Four defects: VSD, overriding aorta, narrow pulmonary outflow, thick right ventricle; blue blood mixes.

items.title: Patent ductus arteriosus
items.caption: The ductus stays open after birth and blood flows from aorta to pulmonary artery.

items.title: Atrial septal defect
items.caption: Blood crosses between atria through a hole and the right heart enlarges.

items.title: Coarctation of the aorta
items.caption: A narrowing beyond the arm vessels: strong arm pulses, weak leg pulses.

items.title: Bronchiolitis
items.caption: RSV infects a baby's small airways, they fill with mucus and breathing becomes hard.

items.title: Croup
items.caption: Virus swells the airway below the vocal cords and makes a barking cough; steroids reduce the swelling.

items.title: Epiglottitis
items.caption: A swollen cherry-red epiglottis blocks the airway; the child sits forward drooling.

items.title: Febrile convulsion
items.caption: A rising fever in a toddler triggers a short generalised seizure that stops by itself.

items.title: Dehydration in children
items.caption: A child loses fluid; oral rehydration solution replaces water and salts through the gut.

items.title: Kawasaki disease
items.caption: A febrile child with red eyes, lips and rash; inflammation affects the coronary arteries; IVIG treats it.

items.title: Developmental milestones
items.caption: A baby at 6 weeks smiles, 6 months sits, 12 months walks, 2 years joins words.

items.title: Childhood vaccines
items.caption: A timeline from birth to 5 years with vaccines given at each visit.

items.title: Eye anatomy
items.caption: Light passes through cornea, pupil and lens to focus on the retina, signals travel along the optic nerve.

items.title: Refractive errors
items.caption: Light focuses in front of the retina in myopia and behind it in hypermetropia; lenses correct it.

items.title: Causes of red eye
items.caption: Conjunctivitis, keratitis, uveitis and acute glaucoma each shown with their key sign.

items.title: Retinal detachment
items.caption: A tear lets fluid lift the retina off the back of the eye, the vision fills with a curtain.

items.title: Age-related macular degeneration
items.caption: Deposits gather under the macula; new leaky vessels grow and bleed; injections block them.

items.title: Central retinal artery occlusion
items.caption: A clot blocks the retinal artery, the retina turns pale with a cherry-red spot.

items.title: Papilloedema
items.caption: Raised brain pressure swells the optic disc, its edges blur.

items.title: Phacoemulsification
items.caption: The cloudy lens is broken up by ultrasound and sucked out, a folded clear lens is placed.

items.title: Ear anatomy and hearing
items.caption: Sound passes the ear canal to the eardrum, the ossicles amplify it and the cochlea turns it into nerve signals.

items.title: Acute otitis media
items.caption: A cold blocks the Eustachian tube, fluid and pus fill the middle ear and the eardrum bulges.

items.title: Glue ear and grommets
items.caption: Sticky fluid stays behind the eardrum; a grommet lets air in and it drains.

items.title: Conductive and sensorineural hearing loss
items.caption: Blocked sound in the outer or middle ear versus damaged cochlea or nerve.

items.title: Inner ear balance
items.caption: The semicircular canals sense turning and the otolith organs sense tilt.

items.title: Nosebleed
items.caption: Bleeding from Little's area at the front of the septum; pinch the soft nose and lean forward.

items.title: Tonsillitis and quinsy
items.caption: Infected tonsils swell; pus collects beside one tonsil, pushing the uvula aside; it is drained.

items.title: Sinusitis
items.caption: The sinus openings block, mucus collects and gets infected.

items.title: Choking and back blows
items.caption: An object blocks the airway; back blows then abdominal thrusts push it out.

items.title: Skin layers
items.caption: Epidermis, dermis and fat beneath with hair follicles, sweat glands and vessels.

items.title: Eczema
items.caption: A weak skin barrier lets water out and irritants in, the skin becomes inflamed; emollients repair it.

items.title: Psoriasis
items.caption: Skin cells grow too fast and build into thick silvery plaques.

items.title: Acne
items.caption: A blocked hair follicle fills with oil, bacteria grow and it inflames.

items.title: Cellulitis
items.caption: Bacteria enter through a break in the skin and spread in the deep layer, causing redness and swelling.

items.title: Melanoma
items.caption: A mole changes in shape and colour, grows down into the skin and can spread.

items.title: Scabies
items.caption: A mite burrows in the skin and lays eggs; itch spreads; permethrin kills it.

items.title: Urticaria
items.caption: Mast cells release histamine and raised itchy wheals appear and fade.

items.title: Pressure ulcer stages
items.caption: Pressure over a bone cuts blood flow, the skin turns red then breaks down layer by layer.

items.title: Fungal skin infection
items.caption: A ring-shaped rash with a clear centre spreads outwards.

items.title: Leprosy
items.caption: Bacteria damage skin and peripheral nerves, patches lose feeling and nerves thicken.

items.title: Depression and monoamines
items.caption: Fewer serotonin and noradrenaline signals between neurons, antidepressants raise them over weeks.

items.title: Anxiety and the stress response
items.caption: A threat activates the amygdala, the body releases adrenaline, the heart races and breathing quickens.

items.title: Panic attack
items.caption: Fast breathing lowers CO2 causing tingling and dizziness; slow breathing settles it.

items.title: Schizophrenia and dopamine
items.caption: Too much dopamine in the mesolimbic pathway causes hallucinations; too little in the frontal area causes apathy.

items.title: Lithium in bipolar disorder
items.caption: Mood swings between mania and depression settle on lithium; its blood level must stay in a narrow range.

items.title: Alcohol withdrawal
items.caption: Alcohol suppresses the brain; when stopped the brain becomes overactive, causing tremor and seizures; benzodiazepines calm it.

items.title: Wernicke's encephalopathy
items.caption: Lack of thiamine damages brain areas around the third ventricle; IV thiamine treats it.

items.title: Delirium
items.caption: An acute illness disturbs brain function, attention fluctuates through the day.

items.title: Alzheimer's dementia
items.caption: Plaques and tangles build up, the hippocampus shrinks and memory fades.

items.title: Opioid dependence and substitution
items.caption: Repeated opioids change brain reward pathways; methadone or buprenorphine gives a steady level.

items.title: Serotonin syndrome
items.caption: Too much serotonin from drug combinations: agitation, clonus, fever.

items.title: Neuroleptic malignant syndrome
items.caption: An antipsychotic blocks dopamine sharply: rigidity, high fever, confusion.

items.title: Refeeding syndrome
items.caption: After starvation, sudden feeding drives phosphate, potassium and magnesium into cells and blood levels crash.

items.title: ADHD and stimulants
items.caption: Stimulants raise dopamine and noradrenaline in the frontal cortex and attention improves.

items.title: Sleep stages
items.caption: A night's sleep cycles through light sleep, deep sleep and REM sleep about every 90 minutes.

items.title: Breastfeeding hormones
items.caption: The baby suckles, the pituitary releases prolactin to make milk and oxytocin to let it flow.

items.title: Uterine massage after birth
items.caption: A soft uterus after birth bleeds; rubbing the fundus makes it contract and bleeding stops.

items.title: Cervical ectropion
items.caption: The inner glandular cells of the cervix show on the outside surface and look red.

items.title: Vaginal thrush
items.caption: Candida overgrows when normal bacteria are reduced; antifungal clears it.

items.title: Cardiac tamponade
items.caption: Fluid fills the pericardial sac, the heart chambers are squeezed and cannot fill, blood pressure falls; a needle drains it.

items.title: Pericarditis
items.caption: Inflamed pericardial layers rub together; the ECG shows saddle-shaped ST elevation in many leads.

items.title: Aortic dissection
items.caption: A tear in the aortic inner wall lets blood split the layers and track along, forming a false lumen.

items.title: Abdominal aortic aneurysm
items.caption: The abdominal aorta balloons wider over years; then it leaks into the back of the abdomen.

items.title: Pacemaker
items.caption: A lead runs through a vein into the right ventricle; when the heart pauses the pacemaker fires and a paced beat follows.

items.title: Defibrillation
items.caption: Chaotic ventricular fibrillation on the heart, a shock passes through it, all cells reset and a normal rhythm returns.

items.title: Long QT and torsades
items.caption: A long QT interval, then the ECG twists around the baseline in torsades; IV magnesium restores rhythm.

items.title: Wolff-Parkinson-White
items.caption: An extra pathway bypasses the AV node, the ventricle starts early making a delta wave.

items.title: Deep vein thrombosis
items.caption: Blood pools in a calf vein, a clot forms and grows, then a piece breaks off towards the lungs.

items.title: Virchow's triad
items.caption: Three panels form a clot: slow flow, damaged vessel wall and sticky blood.

items.title: Varicose veins
items.caption: Healthy valves keep blood moving up the leg vein; failed valves let blood fall back and the vein swells.

items.title: Peripheral arterial disease
items.caption: A narrowed leg artery: at rest flow is enough, on walking the calf muscle runs short of blood and hurts.

items.title: Baroreceptor reflex
items.caption: Blood pressure rises, carotid baroreceptors fire, the brainstem slows the heart and widens vessels.

items.title: Surfactant
items.caption: Surfactant lines the alveoli and keeps small alveoli open; without it they collapse.

items.title: Pleural effusion
items.caption: Fluid collects in the pleural space at the base of the lung and the lung above it is pushed up and squeezed.

items.title: Bronchiectasis
items.caption: Airways become permanently widened and filled with mucus that bacteria grow in, in a repeating cycle.

items.title: Pulmonary fibrosis
items.caption: Lung tissue becomes stiff scar, alveolar walls thicken and oxygen crosses slowly.

items.title: Cystic fibrosis
items.caption: A faulty CFTR channel stops chloride leaving the cell, the mucus becomes thick and blocks the airways.

items.title: Lung volumes
items.caption: A breathing trace shows tidal volume, inspiratory reserve, expiratory reserve and residual volume.

items.title: Spirometry patterns
items.caption: Three flow-volume loops: normal, obstructive (scooped) and restrictive (small).

items.title: Pulse oximetry
items.caption: Red and infrared light pass through a fingertip, oxygenated and deoxygenated haemoglobin absorb differently and a saturation reading appears.

items.title: Type 1 and type 2 respiratory failure
items.caption: In type 1 oxygen is low with normal CO2; in type 2 the breathing fails, oxygen falls and CO2 rises.

items.title: Non-invasive ventilation
items.caption: A mask delivers pressure, alveoli open, breathing work falls and CO2 is cleared.

items.title: Mechanical ventilation and PEEP
items.caption: A ventilator pushes a breath in; PEEP holds the alveoli open at the end of each breath.

items.title: Obstructive sleep apnoea
items.caption: During sleep the throat collapses, breathing stops and oxygen falls; CPAP splints the airway open.

items.title: Aspiration pneumonia
items.caption: Food and stomach contents go down the right main bronchus to the lower lobe and pneumonia forms there.

items.title: COVID-19 pneumonia
items.caption: Virus enters lung cells via ACE2, inflammation spreads and the alveoli fill with fluid.

items.title: The nephron
items.caption: Blood is filtered in the glomerulus, then the filtrate passes the proximal tubule, loop of Henle, distal tubule and collecting duct.

items.title: Countercurrent multiplier
items.caption: The loop of Henle pumps salt out and builds a salty medulla, so the collecting duct can concentrate urine.

items.title: ADH and water balance
items.caption: When blood is concentrated the pituitary releases ADH, water channels open in the collecting duct and water returns to the blood.

items.title: Haemodialysis
items.caption: Blood flows one way past a membrane, dialysate flows the other way, urea and potassium cross into the dialysate.

items.title: Peritoneal dialysis
items.caption: Fluid runs into the abdomen through a catheter, waste crosses the peritoneum into it, then it drains out.

items.title: Kidney transplant
items.caption: A donor kidney is placed in the iliac fossa, joined to the iliac vessels and the bladder, and starts making urine.

items.title: Polycystic kidney disease
items.caption: Both kidneys slowly fill with growing cysts and become large.

items.title: Urinary tract infection
items.caption: Bacteria from the gut climb the urethra into the bladder and up the ureter to the kidney.

items.title: Benign prostatic hyperplasia
items.caption: The prostate enlarges and squeezes the urethra, urine flow weakens and the bladder wall thickens.

items.title: Hypercalcaemia
items.caption: Calcium rises from bone, gut and kidney; treatment with IV fluids and a bisphosphonate brings it down.

items.title: Hypokalaemia on the ECG
items.caption: As potassium falls the ECG shows flat T waves and U waves; potassium replacement corrects it.

items.title: Sodium and water across cells
items.caption: Water moves from low to high concentration: cells swell in low sodium and shrink in high sodium.

items.title: SIADH
items.caption: Too much ADH: the kidney keeps water, blood sodium falls and urine stays concentrated.

items.title: Diabetes insipidus
items.caption: No ADH (cranial) or kidneys ignore it (nephrogenic): large volumes of dilute urine.

items.title: Anion gap
items.caption: A bar chart of sodium against chloride plus bicarbonate; the gap widens when acids like lactate or ketones build up.

items.title: Lactic acidosis
items.caption: Low oxygen in tissues stops aerobic energy making, pyruvate turns to lactate and blood acid rises.

items.title: Pituitary hormones
items.caption: The pituitary sends hormones to each target: thyroid, adrenal, ovary or testis, breast, kidney and whole body growth.

items.title: Cushing's syndrome
items.caption: Too much cortisol: fat gathers on the face and trunk, skin thins, muscles waste, glucose and BP rise.

items.title: Addison's disease
items.caption: The adrenal glands are destroyed, cortisol and aldosterone fall, ACTH rises and the skin darkens.

items.title: Phaeochromocytoma
items.caption: An adrenal tumour releases bursts of adrenaline: the heart races, BP spikes, sweating.

items.title: Primary hyperaldosteronism
items.caption: An adrenal tumour makes aldosterone; the kidney keeps sodium and loses potassium, BP rises.

items.title: Graves' disease
items.caption: Antibodies stimulate the TSH receptor, the thyroid swells and makes too much hormone, the eyes protrude.

items.title: Hypothyroidism
items.caption: The thyroid fails, hormone falls, TSH rises and metabolism slows.

items.title: Thyroid nodule work-up
items.caption: A nodule in the thyroid is checked by ultrasound and a fine needle aspiration.

items.title: Parathyroid hormone
items.caption: Low calcium makes the parathyroids release PTH; PTH acts on bone, kidney and vitamin D to raise calcium.

items.title: Vitamin D activation
items.caption: Sunlight makes vitamin D in skin, the liver and then kidney activate it, and the gut absorbs calcium.

items.title: Osteoporosis
items.caption: Healthy dense bone turns porous with thin struts, and a vertebra collapses.

items.title: Insulin resistance
items.caption: Insulin binds the receptor but the signal fails, glucose stays outside the cell, the pancreas works harder.

items.title: Hyperosmolar hyperglycaemic state
items.caption: Very high glucose pulls water out of cells into the urine, the patient becomes severely dry and confused.

items.title: Diabetic foot ulcer
items.caption: Nerve damage and poor blood flow mean a pressure point on the foot is not felt and an ulcer forms.

items.title: Diabetic nephropathy
items.caption: High glucose damages the glomerulus, protein starts to leak into urine and kidney function falls.

items.title: Swallowing
items.caption: Food is pushed back by the tongue, the soft palate and epiglottis close the airway and the bolus enters the oesophagus.

items.title: Barrett's oesophagus
items.caption: Repeated acid changes the lower oesophagus lining from flat to stomach-like cells, which can become cancer.

items.title: Achalasia
items.caption: The lower oesophageal sphincter fails to relax, food stacks up and the oesophagus widens like a bird's beak.

items.title: Upper GI bleed
items.caption: A bleeding duodenal ulcer, blood fills the stomach; an endoscope clips the vessel.

items.title: Coeliac disease
items.caption: Gluten triggers immune damage, the small bowel villi flatten and nutrients are not absorbed.

items.title: Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis
items.caption: Crohn's shows patchy deep inflammation anywhere in the gut; ulcerative colitis is continuous from the rectum up.

items.title: Irritable bowel syndrome
items.caption: A sensitive gut sends stronger pain signals to the brain and bowel movement speeds or slows.
