items.title: Diverticular disease
items.caption: Pouches bulge out of the sigmoid colon wall; one becomes blocked and inflamed.

items.title: Liver functions
items.caption: The liver makes proteins and clotting factors, clears toxins, stores glucose and makes bile.

items.title: Hepatitis B
items.caption: The virus enters liver cells, the immune system attacks infected cells; some infections become chronic.

items.title: Fatty liver disease
items.caption: Fat droplets fill the liver cells, inflammation begins and scarring follows.

items.title: Ascites
items.caption: Portal pressure rises and albumin falls, fluid leaks into the abdomen; a paracentesis drains it.

items.title: Hepatic encephalopathy
items.caption: The failing liver does not clear ammonia, which reaches the brain and causes confusion.

items.title: Bile production and flow
items.caption: Bile from the liver is stored in the gallbladder and squeezed into the duodenum after a fatty meal.

items.title: ERCP and stone removal
items.caption: An endoscope at the duodenal papilla, a cut opens the duct and a balloon sweeps the stone out.

items.title: Pancreas functions
items.caption: Exocrine cells release digestive enzymes into the duodenum, islet cells release insulin and glucagon into the blood.

items.title: Chronic pancreatitis
items.caption: Repeated inflammation scars the pancreas, ducts fill with stones, enzymes and insulin fall.

items.title: Digestion and absorption
items.caption: Carbohydrate, protein and fat are broken down along the gut and absorbed by the small bowel villi.

items.title: Gut hormones
items.caption: Food in the duodenum releases CCK and secretin; the gallbladder contracts and pancreas releases bicarbonate.

items.title: Hypothermia
items.caption: Core temperature falls, the heart slows and becomes irritable, and the body shivers then stops.

items.title: Heat stroke
items.caption: Heat builds faster than sweating can lose it, the core temperature rises and organs fail.

items.title: Body fluid compartments
items.caption: Body water divided into inside cells, between cells and in the blood; drip fluids spread differently.

items.title: Starling forces in capillaries
items.caption: Fluid leaves the capillary at the arterial end and returns at the venous end; oedema when pressure rises.

items.title: Oxygen delivery
items.caption: Oxygen delivery depends on cardiac output, haemoglobin and saturation, shown as three rising dials.

items.title: Hepatitis C and direct-acting antivirals
items.caption: Hepatitis C virus copies itself in liver cells; sofosbuvir blocks its polymerase and the virus is cleared.

items.title: Haemochromatosis
items.caption: The gut absorbs too much iron, which builds up in liver, heart and pancreas; venesection removes it.

items.title: Wilson's disease
items.caption: Copper cannot leave the liver in bile, it builds up in liver and brain and forms a brown ring in the cornea.

items.title: Upper and lower motor neuron signs
items.caption: Upper: stiff, brisk reflexes; lower: floppy, wasted, absent reflexes.

items.title: Cranial nerves
items.caption: The twelve cranial nerves leave the brainstem to the eyes, face, mouth and neck.

items.title: Bell's palsy
items.caption: The facial nerve swells in its bony canal and one side of the face droops including the forehead.

items.title: Focal and generalised seizures
items.caption: A seizure starts in one area and stays there, or involves both sides at once.

items.title: Parkinson's disease
items.caption: Dopamine neurons in the substantia nigra are lost, movement becomes slow, stiff and tremulous.

items.title: Multiple sclerosis
items.caption: Immune cells strip myelin off nerves in the brain and cord, signals slow and patches form.

items.title: Migraine
items.caption: The trigeminal nerve releases inflammatory peptides around brain vessels; triptans calm it.

items.title: Bacterial meningitis
items.caption: Bacteria cross into the meninges, they swell, and the neck becomes stiff; antibiotics start early.

items.title: Viral encephalitis
items.caption: Herpes virus infects the temporal lobes, causing confusion and seizures; aciclovir treats it.

items.title: Brain tumour
items.caption: A tumour grows inside the skull, swelling builds and pressure rises; steroids reduce the swelling.

items.title: Glasgow Coma Scale
items.caption: Three parts scored: eye opening, verbal response and best motor response.

items.title: Brainstem reflexes
items.caption: Tests of pupil, corneal, gag and breathing reflexes, each checked in turn.

items.title: Peripheral neuropathy
items.caption: Longest nerves in the feet are damaged first, numbness spreads in a stocking pattern.

items.title: Motor neurone disease
items.caption: Both upper and lower motor neurons die, muscles weaken and twitch.

items.title: Blood cell formation
items.caption: A stem cell in the marrow gives rise to red cells, white cells and platelets.

items.title: Anaemia by cell size
items.caption: Small cells (iron lack), normal-size cells (blood loss, chronic disease), large cells (B12, folate).

items.title: Haemolytic anaemia
items.caption: Red cells break apart early in the blood and spleen, bilirubin rises and the marrow works harder.

items.title: Thalassaemia
items.caption: Too few globin chains, red cells are small and fragile; repeated transfusion is needed.

items.title: G6PD deficiency
items.caption: Oxidant drugs or beans damage red cells that cannot protect themselves and they burst.

items.title: Haemophilia
items.caption: Factor VIII is missing, clots form weakly and joints fill with blood; factor replacement stops it.

items.title: Immune thrombocytopenia
items.caption: Antibodies coat platelets and the spleen removes them, tiny bleeding spots appear on skin.

items.title: Thrombotic microangiopathy
items.caption: Tiny clots in small vessels shred red cells and use up platelets, the kidney is damaged.

items.title: Acute leukaemia
items.caption: Immature blast cells crowd the marrow, normal blood cells fall.

items.title: Lymphoma
items.caption: Cancerous lymphocytes grow in lymph nodes, they swell painlessly and spread to other nodes.

items.title: Multiple myeloma
items.caption: Plasma cells multiply in the marrow, make abnormal protein and punch holes in bone.

items.title: Polycythaemia
items.caption: Too many red cells thicken the blood and clots form; venesection reduces them.

items.title: Neutropenic sepsis
items.caption: After chemotherapy neutrophils fall, bacteria spread quickly; antibiotics within an hour.

items.title: Blood transfusion checks
items.caption: Patient, blood bag and wristband are checked together before transfusion.

items.title: Transfusion reactions
items.caption: Fever, allergy, fluid overload and haemolysis shown as different reactions.

items.title: Hallmarks of cancer
items.caption: A cell grows without stop signals, avoids death, builds new vessels and spreads.

items.title: Tumour angiogenesis
items.caption: A tumour releases VEGF, new vessels grow towards it; an antibody blocks VEGF and vessels fade.

items.title: Radiotherapy
items.caption: Beams from several angles meet at the tumour, breaking its DNA while sparing surrounding tissue.

items.title: Tumour lysis syndrome
items.caption: Treatment kills many cancer cells at once, they spill potassium, phosphate and uric acid, the kidneys strain.

items.title: Malignant spinal cord compression
items.caption: A cancer in a vertebra presses on the spinal cord; steroids and radiotherapy relieve it.

items.title: Superior vena cava obstruction
items.caption: A chest tumour squeezes the SVC, the face and arms swell and neck veins bulge.

items.title: Prostate cancer
items.caption: A tumour in the outer prostate, PSA rises and it can spread to bones.

items.title: Liver cancer
items.caption: A cancer grows in a cirrhotic liver and alpha-fetoprotein rises.

items.title: Thyroid cancer
items.caption: A nodule grows and spreads to neck nodes; radioactive iodine seeks out remaining cells.

items.title: Pain control ladder
items.caption: Three steps: simple analgesia, weak opioid, strong opioid, each with adjuvants.

items.title: Innate and adaptive immunity
items.caption: Neutrophils and macrophages respond first; then T and B cells give a specific, remembered response.

items.title: Antibody structure and classes
items.caption: A Y-shaped antibody binds an antigen at its arms; IgM, IgG, IgA and IgE shown.

items.title: Complement
items.caption: Proteins coat a bacterium, attract white cells and punch holes in its wall.

items.title: Hypersensitivity types
items.caption: Four types: IgE allergy, antibody against cells, immune complexes, T cell delayed.

items.title: Autoimmunity
items.caption: The immune system mistakes a body tissue for foreign and attacks it.

items.title: Transplant rejection
items.caption: T cells recognise the donor organ as foreign and attack it; immunosuppression holds them back.

items.title: Systemic lupus erythematosus
items.caption: Immune complexes deposit in skin, joints and kidneys, causing rash and inflammation.

items.title: Vasculitis
items.caption: Immune cells inflame vessel walls, which narrow and the tissue beyond suffers.

items.title: Giant cell arteritis
items.caption: The temporal artery becomes inflamed and thick, and can block the eye's artery; steroids start quickly.
